parts.text: In which set-up should the bean seeds germinate?

options.text: Set-up 1 only, because germination needs the right amount of water and air; light is not required.
Set-up 2 only, because seeds need dry cotton and sunlight to germinate.
Set-up 3 only, because seeds germinate best when fully waterlogged.
Set-ups 1 and 3, because any wet set-up works even without air.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Anaya keeps bean seeds in three set-ups: Set-up 1 has moist cotton with air spaces in a closed drawer. Set-up 2 has dry cotton in sunlight. Set-up 3 has seeds fully submerged in a jar of water with almost no air.

part_answers.answer: Bean seeds need moisture and air to germinate; they can do so in the dark. Dry cotton lacks water, and fully submerged seeds lack enough air.

teacher.key_rationale: Germination needs suitable water and air; light is not required for these bean seeds. Dry cotton and waterlogged jars without air fail those conditions.
